**5. Guidance on figures or plots**
Yes, but only as the one-line descriptions of two skills in the skill listing. I haven't loaded the full instructions for either.

- **better-figures:figures**: "Use before making any figure a person will read, such as a matplotlib or seaborn plot, a chart in a report or slide, or a diagram of a method or pipeline, and when designing the figures in an experiment spec. It covers choosing what to show, keeping text out of the image, a matplotlib house style with direct labels and a check that runs on save, HTML routes for interactive figures on a page and for diagrams, each with a PNG for slides, and the summary figure (Figure 1) that shows an idea, its method and its result with examples and cartoons. Not for dashboards."
- **dataviz**: "Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. …" Its description goes on to cover palettes, a color validator, mark specs and interaction rules, and points to `references/palette.md`.

Both descriptions say to load the skill before writing any plotting code, and their scopes overlap. better-figures excludes dashboards, while dataviz covers them.
